findings.title: TD3 production-line comparison re-spells `127.0.0.1` instead of reading it from the cluster table
findings.description: `strip_new_args()` removes the arguments 227 adds to production's lines by stripping `f" --url-key {url_key}"` (parameterized), `f" --remote {bucket_remote} --dest"` (parameterized), but ` --replication-host 127.0.0.1` is a hardcoded literal (line 87). `127.0.0.1` is a value owned by `deploy/backup-clusters.conf` (the `17/main` row's `replication_host` column) and by the `BackupCluster.replication_host` field that `cutover_227_host.Context` already carries on `ctx.main`. This is the "one value, one source" rule from AGENTS.md: the comparison that proves "production's lines changed only by the new arguments" (step 4 / `test_production_lines_gain_only_the_new_arguments`) is coupled to a table value it does not read. Today the table says `127.0.0.1` so the cutover passes, but if `17/main`'s `replication_host` ever changed, `step_apply`'s `production_changes()` would report a spurious diff and stop the cutover with a false failure. The test's `_NEW_MAIN_ARGS` hardcodes the same literal, so the test would not catch that divergence either. Pass `ctx.main.replication_host` into the strip (and mirror it in the test) so the comparison is driven by the table.

findings.title: Step 6 waits for `pg_walfile_name(pg_switch_wal())` — confirm that names the just-archived segment, not the newly-opened one
findings.description: `step_switch` computes `segment = psql(TICK, "SELECT pg_walfile_name(pg_switch_wal())")` and then polls for `wal/<segment>.zst` up to `WAL_SWITCH_WAIT_S` (≈ lines 147–152). The correctness of step 6 hinges on `pg_walfile_name(pg_switch_wal())` yielding the segment that `archive_command` is about to write. `pg_switch_wal()` returns "the LSN of the first byte past the last one written," and it is a known gotcha that this LSN can land in the *newly-opened* segment (the one that just started, which will not be archived for hours) rather than the just-closed segment that is archived within seconds. I could not execute PostgreSQL to confirm which `pg_walfile_name` returns here, so I'm marking this unverified rather than asserting a bug — but the impact if it is the latter is that step 6 false-fails at the 120 s bound on every run (the cutover can never complete step 6 on a healthy host), and no test covers the segment-name mapping (`test_wal_wait_gives_up_at_the_bound` only pins the poll bound). The unambiguous idiom is to capture the pre-switch segment — `pg_walfile_name(pg_current_wal_lsn())` before calling `pg_switch_wal()` — and wait for that. Please confirm the mapping on the live cluster before the PM runs the cutover; if it yields the new segment, switch to capturing the pre-switch LSN.

findings.title: The cutover's `sudo` surface is wider than the `manta-ops` allowlist
findings.description:
The cutover runs as `manta` and elevates via plain `sudo` for several commands: `sudo deploy/setup-backup.sh` (`setup_backup`, lines ~60–64), `sudo scripts/provision_tick_cluster.sh` (`step_provision`), `sudo systemctl restart postgresql@17-tick` (`step_restart`), `sudo -u postgres … psql` (`psql`, ~line 54), and `sudo sha256sum` (`conf_sums`). None of these are in `deploy/sudoers.d/manta-ops` (which only allowlists the Kalshi cutover's commands, and `manta ALL=(manta-trading)` for `MT_GIT`). This therefore relies on `manta` having general sudo (a password prompt on each escalation). That's consistent with the runbook ("asks for sudo for the root steps") and the 920 precedent where the PM ran `sudo deploy/setup-backup.sh`, so it is not a defect in this diff — but it means the 227 cutover is not covered by the narrow `manta-ops` file and will prompt for the sudo password several times in a single run. Worth a one-line confirmation that `manta`'s sudo privileges on manta9000 are intended to cover this; no code change needed otherwise.

Overall: the diff is consistent, the shell quoting/placeholder/percent guards are correct, and the test suite is thorough (rendered-file comparison against the real pre-227 fixture, lifecycle exit-code invariance, never-sets-a-rule, table parse-before-act, pg_lsclusters-driven data dirs). Address the two concerns — particularly verify step 6's segment-name mapping before the PM runs the cutover — and this is in good shape.
